title: Redundant `import os` inside _compile_preamble shadows the module-level import with the same module
description: Line 428 executes `import os` inside _compile_preamble even though `os` is already imported at module scope (line 22) and is referenced elsewhere in the module (e.g. _positive_int_from_env at line 92, _compile_preamble_cached/_exec via cwd). The local statement re-binds the identical module object to the same name with no effect and no shadowing benefit — nothing in the function between its start (380) and line 428 rebinds or deletes `os`. It is leftover from an earlier refactor (the surrounding comment about 'spawned by uvicorn reload' refers to behaviour now handled by _prioritise_preamble_import_paths).
evidence: Module top: line 22 `import os`. Inside _compile_preamble: line 428 `import os` then line 430 `cwd = os.getcwd()`. The module-level `os` is already in scope and usable; the function-local import is a no-op rebind to the same module.
behavior_preservation: Removing line 428 leaves `os` resolved to the module-level import; `os.getcwd()` on line 430 behaves identically.
